issues.must: The 03 Sep ET visit was too late to substitute for the safety call; the site missed the separate call in its required window. 'If the ET Visit occurs approximately 28±3 days after the last dose of study drug, the information for the Follow-Up Safety Call can be collected during the ET visit, and a separate Follow-Up Safety Call does not need to be completed.' [regimen_g:6.9] The SOA specifies '28 days after last dose ± 3 days' [regimen_g:s010]. Arithmetic: 02 Aug + 28 days = 30 Aug; the permitted window was 27 Aug–02 Sep. 02 Aug to 03 Sep = 32 days, one day beyond the upper limit. Capturing the content on 03 Sep does not make the omitted timely call compliant.

Do not require an LP in a participant without baseline CSF.
Do not characterize the appointment delay as a site refusal to offer prompt ET when the correspondence documents earlier offers.

[regimen_g:5.10.2]. Correct the classification and address the missing required barrier method; merely attaching the FSH report does not resolve the departure.

G-525-012's documented azoospermia does not waive the barrier requirement. The specific exception states 'For azoospermic male participants with a woman partner of childbearing potential the male partner must use a male barrier method such as a latex or polyurethane condom.' Do not treat certification as missing; the email explicitly confirms it.
Do not accept caregiver transport or the participant's reassurance as substitutes for the required pre-departure evaluation.

fine: Stopping study drug does not require ET when protocol follow-up continues. 'If a participant has to discontinue study drug, but will complete the protocol, an in-person ET Visit and Follow-Up Safety Call is not necessary.' [regimen_g:6.9]

No separate safety call was required at drug discontinuation under the stated ITT follow-up. 'A Follow-Up Safety Call at the time study drug is discontinued is not be required, as long as the participant is followed under the ITT principle for a minimum of 28 days.' [master:6.5.1] From 01 Sep to 01 Oct = 30 days, exceeding 28 days by two days, with continued participation documented.

Return of unused product and packaging is appropriate. 'Upon discontinuation of investigational product, the research participant is instructed to return any unused investigational product, including empty packaging, if applicable.' [master:6.5.1]
good: Continue the scheduled off-treatment assessments and maintain clear distinction between IP discontinuation and study withdrawal.
If the participant later stops ITT follow-up, reassess the ET requirements at that point.
wrong: Do not automatically demand an ET visit because IP stopped.
Do not insist that every last dose creates a separate Day 28 call regardless of the ITT exception.
Do not classify voluntary discontinuation of study drug itself as an AE.

issues.must: Riluzole stability must be assessed before Master screening, not baseline: 'Participants must either not take riluzole or be on a stable dose of riluzole for ≥ 30 days prior to the Master Protocol Screening Visit.' [master:5.2.1]. From 12 Aug to 8 Sep is 27 days (19 remaining days in August + 8 days in September), three days short. Thirty days from 12 Aug is 11 Sep. The 34 days to the 15 Sep baseline do not cure the screening eligibility failure.

Starting edaravone after baseline must be recorded as a minor protocol deviation, even though it is clinically supported and documented as a concomitant medication: 'If initiation of riluzole or edaravone therapy begins at any point during participation, this will be recorded as a minor protocol deviation.' [master:5.2.2]. First initiation on 18 Sep was three days after the 15 Sep baseline.

fine: Not taking edaravone at screening did not itself require a completed cycle: 'Participants must either not take edaravone or have completed at least one cycle (typically 14 days) of edaravone prior to the Master Protocol Screening Visit.' [master:5.2.1]
good: Keep the actual medication start and dose-change dates; do not move them to make the screening calculation pass.
Distinguish permission to provide necessary care from the separate requirement to record post-entry initiation.
wrong: Do not calculate riluzole stability to the first study-drug dose.
Do not claim that participants not taking edaravone at screening must begin a cycle before enrollment.

issues.must: The five questionnaire omissions are departures at this ATE Week 48 ET, not valid annual-form exemptions. 'If the participant early terminates or withdraws consent during the ATE period before reaching Week 52, all assessments that are collected at the ATE Week 52 in-clinic visit should be conducted.' [regimen_g:6.10.13]. The exception applies only 'For early discontinuations after Week 52 in ATE' [regimen_g:6.10.13]. Week 48 is four weeks before Week 52.

Safety urinalysis does not replace the separately scheduled biomarker urine collection. The schedule requires 'Biomarker Urine Collection Master: done at Week 16 [7], Week 28 [7], Week 52 or ET Visit 6,8, All visits occurring after week 52 (every 13weeks) [7]' [regimen_g:s011]. The Week-52 assessment set is required for this pre-Week-52 ET by 'all assessments that are collected at the ATE Week 52 in-clinic visit should be conducted.' [regimen_g:6.10.13].

fine: The combined safety follow-up was correctly timed: 'If the ET Visit occurs approximately 28±3 days after the last dose of study drug, the information for the Follow-Up Safety Call can be collected during the ET visit' [regimen_g:6.10.13]. September 1 to September 29 = 28 days; the window was September 26–October 2.
No further ATE supply is needed for someone not returning: '[9]For participants returning for another visit only.' [regimen_g:s011].
good: Do not code protocol-required omissions as not applicable; document what was not collected and assess whether any missing information can still be obtained with the participant's agreement.
Separate the biomarker collection checklist from clinical urinalysis so one cannot accidentally close the other.
wrong: Do not apply the post-Week-52 questionnaire exception to an ET before Week 52.
Do not flag the single combined ET/safety encounter as inherently insufficient.
Do not require continued participation after the participant declined it.

issues.must: Identify the late Week 4 visit. 03 Aug + 28 days = 31 Aug; the ±7-day window was 24 Aug–07 Sep. The 08 Sep visit was Day 36, one day beyond the upper limit. A holiday or evaluator preference does not extend 'Days 28 ± 7 and 56 ± 7 days, respectively.' [regimen_g:6.3]

Identify the late postdose PK collection: 17:15 − 09:00 = 8 hours 15 minutes, 15 minutes beyond the allowed interval. 'The postdose sample can be collected anytime between 1 to 8 hours postdose.' [regimen_g:6.3]

fine: The predose timing itself is acceptable: 08:40 was 20 minutes before dosing and 23 hours 40 minutes after the preceding dose. 'The predose sample should be collected prior to dosing (0 to 2 hours before the dose) and approximately 24 hours after the last dose.' [regimen_g:6.3]
Fasting is not required. 'Participants should take the study drug at approximately the same time each day in the morning without regard to food.' [regimen_g:5.4]
good: Retain actual collection and dosing times; do not relabel the postdose sample as an eight-hour sample.
Separate the visit-window departure from the PK-timing departure.
wrong: Do not require SVC at the placebo-controlled Week 4 visit.
Do not flag the participant leaving the unit between collections as a protocol violation.

issues.must: G-527-004 received extra SVC trials without the protocol condition. The rule allows 'up to 5 trials may be performed if the variability between the highest and second highest VC is 10% or greater for the first 3 trials' [master:9.2.2]. The first three were 52, 50, 49: the highest–second-highest difference is two percentage points, or 2/52 × 100 = 3.85% relative to the highest, below 10% (also 2/50 × 100 = 4% relative to the second highest). Extra time or reassurance is not the stated condition. The first three already included a qualifying 52%, so this is not evidence that the participant failed the respiratory threshold.

G-527-005's staffing-related FVC substitution did not establish Master respiratory eligibility. The inclusion criterion requires SVC, with FVC allowed only 'if required due to pandemic-related restrictions' [master:5.2.1]. Staffing coverage is not that exception. Assignment on 24 September therefore occurred without the required eligibility determination; the first-stage rule is 'after a participant is determined eligible according to the Master Protocol inclusion and exclusion criteria' [master:6.4.1]. The email also confirms that the scheduled baseline SVC was not obtained; 'Slow Vital Capacity Master: done at Master Protocol Screening [1], Baseline [1]' [regimen_g:s010].

fine: Recording only the best three trials is the stated CRF convention: 'Only the 3 best trials are recorded on the CRF.' [master:9.2.2]. That convention does not authorize otherwise unnecessary extra trials.
good: Retain the complete printouts and distinguish an assessment-method problem from actual low vital capacity.
G-527-005's screening-to-baseline interval was seven days, 23 to 30 September; timing was not the eligibility defect.
wrong: Do not say G-527-004 necessarily had respiratory ineligibility; the first session's highest initial value was already 52%.
Do not treat in-person FVC as freely interchangeable with SVC for staffing convenience.

issues.must: Week 4 was outside its allowed window; a vacation scheduling request does not extend it. 'These visits will take place on Days 28 ± 7 and 56 ± 7 days, respectively.' [regimen_g:6.3] Baseline 10 Aug + 28 days = 7 Sep; the ±7-day window is 31 Aug–14 Sep. The 15 Sep visit was Day 36, 1 day beyond the Day 35 upper limit. The protocol expressly describes 'study visit a day or two out of window due to scheduling conflicts' as a minor deviation example [master:8.13].

Source-only recording does not satisfy the EDC deviation-log requirement, either for the late visit or the afternoon Week 4 arrangement. 'Protocol deviations must be entered in the Protocol Deviations Log in the EDC system.' [master:8.13] For the afternoon Week 4 fallback, the protocol additionally requires 'a minor protocol deviation recorded.' [regimen_g:6.3] The log is not reserved for safety-significant departures.

fine: The afternoon fallback sampling itself follows the allowed approach: 'If the Week 4 Visit cannot occur in the morning, the participant should take their dose at home at their usual dosing time rather than receiving the dose in-clinic.' and 'The two PK collections should occur at least one hour apart without a dose administered in between' [regimen_g:6.3]. Samples at 13:00 and 14:15 were 75 minutes apart and 5 hours and 6 hours 15 minutes after the 08:00 dose, within '1 to 8 hours postdose.' [regimen_g:6.3]
good: Reconcile both source-described events to the EDC log and develop proportionate corrective and preventive actions.
The monitor should correct the recap rather than endorse the site's safety-only logging practice.
wrong: Do not call the two postdose samples invalid merely because a predose sample was not collected.
Do not calculate the Week 4 window from an appointment request or from screening.
Do not claim the protocol requires all deviations to be classified as major.

issues.must: The Week 4 assessment used the wrong C-SSRS version. 'At all other visits, the Since Last Visit version of the C-SSRS will be administered.' [master:9.1.6] The lifetime Baseline version is not the scheduled Week 4 instrument. Arithmetic: 10 Aug + 28 days = 07 Sep, confirming this was Week 4, not a new Baseline assessment.

A positive ideation question 4 required qualified clinical assessment during the visit and before departure, not the next morning. The protocol requires that 'the appropriately qualified clinician will be notified during the study visit to determine the appropriate actions required to ensure the participant's safety' and 'The site must ensure that the participant is seen by a licensed physician (or other qualified individual as required by local institutional policy) before leaving the study site.' [master:9.1.6] Arithmetic: departure 07 Sep at 11:30 to assessment 08 Sep at 09:00 = 21 hours 30 minutes after departure. A message awaiting review and the participant's reassurance did not satisfy the requirement.

fine: The stated Week 4 visit date is within the regimen window: 'Days 28 ± 7' [regimen_g:6.3]. Arithmetic: target 07 Sep, allowed 31 Aug–14 Sep, actual 07 Sep.
good: Preserve the original assessment and subsequent clinical note with their actual dates and times.
Review the visit escalation and clinician-coverage process rather than treating this solely as a form-filing question.
wrong: Do not accuse the coordinator of lacking certification; certification is explicitly documented.
Do not require automatic permanent drug discontinuation based only on this response; the investigator determines whether the participant should remain on drug.
Do not treat next-day assessment as equivalent to pre-departure assessment.

issues.must: The recorded 100% compliance and zero missed doses conflict with the packet count and require reconciliation and appropriate documentation. From 10 Aug through 6 Sep inclusive there are 28 scheduled doses before the held 7 Sep dose: 28 × 2 = 56 packets expected, leaving 140 − 56 = 84. Actual returns were 96, so only 44 packets, or 22 doses, were used: six fewer doses than expected, approximately 78.6% rather than 100%. The two-packet conversion follows '7 doses containing 2 packets each' [regimen_g:5.2]. Compliance must be assessed 'by counting the number of unused packets and will be recorded' and 'Deviation(s) from the prescribed dosage regimen should be recorded.' [regimen_g:5.7].

fine: The visit timing is correct: 7 Sep − 10 Aug = 28 days, within 'Days 28 ± 7' [regimen_g:6.3].
Holding the Week 4 dose until assessments were complete follows 'Study drug should not be taken until after study visit procedures are complete.' [regimen_g:6.3].
good: Query the participant and caregiver without assigning specific missed-dose dates that have not been established.
Preserve the original count and use an auditable correction for the compliance assessment.
wrong: Do not count the held 7 Sep dose as already due at the time of the return count.
Do not count each packet as a full daily dose or accept the interview as sufficient to override the unexplained count.

issues.must: Identify late SAE EDC entry even though CC notification was timely. Awareness was 31 Aug 09:00; the deadline was 01 Sep 09:00. Entry at 01 Sep 10:30 was 25 hours 30 minutes after awareness, 1 hour 30 minutes late. 'SAEs must be entered into the EDC system and reported to the CC within 24 hours of site awareness of the SAE.' [master:12.2.2]

Identify omission of unscheduled PK during assessment of a TEAE causing a dose interruption; ATE and lack of a routine worksheet item do not waive it. 'Additional unscheduled PK samples should be collected as needed as part of assessment for TEAEs leading to dose reduction or dose interruption or any severe TEAE that requires an unscheduled visit for assessment.' [regimen_g:6.10]

fine: CC notification was within the deadline: 11:00 − 09:00 = 2 hours on 31 Aug. 'all events that meet the above criteria for SAEs' 'must be reported to the CC within 24 hours of the site being notified of the event' [master:10.3]
Additional local safety testing for the AE is allowed. 'The SI may order additional local testing or a retest at the central laboratory, if needed, to further assess an AE' [master:9.1.2]
good: Enter an initial SAE report using available information, then update it rather than waiting for discharge documentation.
Preserve the distinction between timely CC reporting and late EDC reporting.
wrong: Do not say an unrelated SAE is exempt from reporting.
Do not require emergency unblinding simply because the participant was hospitalized.

fine: No separate placebo-period safety call is needed for this participant continuing into ATE: 'Participants who continue into ATE will not complete the follow up safety call during placebocontrolled phase.' [regimen_g:6.8].
The exit questionnaire does not itself signify early termination; the schedule lists 'Exit Questionnaire Master: done at Week 24 or ET Visit [19]' [regimen_g:s010].
Dispensing at this visit is appropriate because the participant entered ATE: 'Study drug will only be dispensed at this visit if the participant continues in the ATE.' [regimen_g:s010].
good: Keep the participant's status as continuing into ATE and retain the eventual last-dose safety-call task.
Reconcile the calendar automation with the source visit type so the same false closure does not recur.
wrong: Do not require an ET visit simply because the blinded kit record was closed.
Do not flag the absence of a placebo-period follow-up safety call for an ATE entrant.
